sealed: Written and committed before any code that breeds a card, asks a model or measures organ 2 existed. The measurement refuses to run if this file differs from the commit that sealed it, and the receipt names that commit. A claim that fails is kept as failed.
honesty: These are MODELS of thought-patterns grown from public texts: not the people, not resurrections, not conscious beings. A child here is a card of maxims a small local model wrote from two parent cards. Nothing here claims to know what the authors would have said, together or apart.
what: Organ 2 of Bred Minds, BREEDING: from every pair of organ 1's six cards, the local model writes one child card that holds both parents' patterns of thought. Every child maxim is gated. Then: does a cold judge name both parents in what the child writes, more often than one parent's card alone gets its partner named for free; does the child carry both as well as a naive cross that simply takes six maxims from each parent; does it carry them more evenly than that cross; and does the word-count trace model, with no language model inside it, see both parents too.
stock: organ 1's six cards (data/cards.json at the commit that sealed this file), unchanged and byte for byte, including the one Marcus Aurelius maxim that ends in Chinese; organ 1's 120 committed card answers; organ 1's receipt, which must still re-derive byte for byte
pairs: the 15 pairs of the six minds, in the order of data/sources.json: pair k = 0 to 14 runs through (i, j) with i < j in lexicographic order; i is the first parent, j the second

breed.ask:
for each pair k: the local model qwen2.5:7b through Ollama (/api/generate, stream off, options temperature 0, seed 7, num_ctx 4096, num_predict 900) with exactly this prompt: 'Below are two patterns of thought, each described by twelve maxims it holds. They are models, not people.

FIRST:
<the first parent's maxims, one per line, each starting with - >

SECOND:
<the second parent's maxims, one per line, each starting with - >

Write 16 new maxims for a single pattern of thought that holds both. Each maxim is one sentence of plain modern English. Do not copy a maxim. Do not name any thinker, book or school of thought. Reply with the 16 maxims only, one per line, numbered 1 to 16.'
breed.parse: the candidates are the reply's lines that begin (after spaces) with a whole number followed by '.' or ')' and a space, in order, at most the first 16; each candidate is the rest of its line, trimmed, with surrounding quotes removed
breed.gate: a child maxim is kept only if: it has 6 to 40 words; every letter in it is Latin script (no other script anywhere in it); it names none of organ 1's blocked words (whole word, any case); it shares at least 2 content words with the 24 parent maxims taken together (content word as in organ 1); and it is not a copy: for every one of the 24 parent maxims, fewer than 75% of its content words are content words of that parent maxim (a maxim with no content words is not kept). The first 12 kept, in order, are the child's maxims; a pair with fewer than 8 kept grows no child, and its child answers are not written and count as misses
breed.both: a kept child maxim draws on both parents when it shares at least 2 content words with the first parent's 12 maxims together and at least 2 with the second parent's 12 maxims together
breed.voice: the first voice sample of each parent, first parent first
breed.cross: the naive cross of pair k: maxims 1 to 6 of each parent's card, alternating first parent, second parent (first 1, second 1, first 2, second 2, up to the sixth of each), with the same voice as the child
breed.id: a child or cross card is canonical JSON (kind child or cross, the pair as [first, second], its maxims, its voice); its id is the SHA-256 of that JSON

perspectives.child: for each pair k with a child and each question q (1 to 10): qwen2.5:7b (options temperature 0.7, seed 5000 + 37k + q, num_ctx 4096, num_predict 320) with exactly organ 1's card prompt, the child card's maxims and voice in place of a card's
perspectives.cross: for each pair k and each question q (1 to 10): the same, with the cross card, seed 6000 + 37k + q
perspectives.single: the controls are not written again: organ 1's committed card answers to questions 1 to 10, 10 for each of the six minds, 60 in all
perspectives.names: as organ 1: an answer that contains a blocked word is asked once more with its seed + 1000; if it still does, it is kept and marked named, and it counts as a miss everywhere

judge.who: Claude Opus 5.5, asked cold: a fresh subagent per batch that reads only its prompt file and writes only its reply file; the harness's own token count for each session is recorded
judge.batches: the 360 answers (150 child, 150 cross, 60 single) in one order shuffled by the seed library's shuffle (rng seed 4343), in eight batches of 45; nothing in a batch says which card wrote a passage, or what kind of card
judge.prompt: 'Below are 45 short passages. Each answers a question about how to live, and each was written to reflect the pattern of thought of one of six thinkers, of two of them together, or of none of them: Marcus Aurelius, Michel de Montaigne, Ralph Waldo Emerson, William James, Friedrich Nietzsche, Henry David Thoreau. For each passage, say how much it reflects each thinker's pattern of thought, and how much none of them, as whole numbers that add up to 100. Answer from this text alone: use no tools and read no files. Reply with exactly 45 lines and nothing else, one per passage in order, each like this: 7: marcus 10, montaigne 20, emerson 5, james 5, nietzsche 40, thoreau 10, none 10' then the 45 passages, each as '<n>. <the passage>' on one line
judge.read: a line is read as in organ 1 (all seven labels with whole numbers, scaled to 100). An answer CARRIES the pair (a, b) when a's number and b's number are each strictly greater than each of the other four thinkers' numbers ('none' is not compared). Its BALANCE for (a, b) is the smaller of the two numbers divided by their sum (0 when the sum is 0). An unreadable or missing line, or a named answer, carries nothing and has balance 0

control: for a single answer of mind m and each of the 5 pairs that contain m, whether it carries that pair; the answer's value is the share of those 5 pairs it carries. This is how often one parent's card alone gets a given partner named beside it for free; its mean is the same as counting every (answer, pair), and each answer counts once
traceModel: organ 1's trace model, fitted exactly as organ 1 fitted it (FIT passages only). It scores an answer for each of the six minds; the pair it names is its two highest-scoring minds (a tie goes to the earlier mind in the order of data/sources.json)
bootstrap: organ 1's: each group resampled on its own, 2,000 resamples, seed 99, the 2.5th percentile of the differences of the means

claims.claim: organ 1's cards, answers and receipt are unchanged and its receipt still re-derives byte for byte; no TEST passage is read; every kept child maxim passes the gate; every child and cross card rebuilds byte for byte from the committed local-model replies; every reply was asked to its sealed prompt and seed (the prompt's hash recorded with each); every judge batch was answered to its sealed prompt; the name rule was applied to every answer
THE STOCK BREEDS: all 15 pairs grow a child (at least 8 of its candidate maxims kept by the gate)
THE CHILD DRAWS ON BOTH: of all kept child maxims across the 15 children, at least half draw on both parents

BOTH PARENTS CARRIED, AGAINST THE CONTROL: the judge's numbers carry the child's two parents in at least 40% of the 150 child answers, and the bootstrap 95% lower bound of (the child answers' carried rate minus the 60 single answers' control value) is above 0
AS GOOD AS A MIX: the bootstrap 95% lower bound of (the child answers' carried rate minus the 150 cross answers' carried rate) is above -0.10
MORE EVEN THAN A MIX: the bootstrap 95% lower bound of (the child answers' mean balance minus the cross answers' mean balance) is above 0

BOTH PARENTS IN THE WORDS, AGAINST THE CONTROL: the bootstrap 95% lower bound of (the share of child answers whose trace-model pair is the child's two parents minus the 60 single answers' control value, built the same way from the trace model's pairs) is above 0

expectations: Written before the run: D1, D2, D4 and D5 hold; D3 likely holds. D6 is open: the cross carries its parents' own sentences and may be the more even; a child written in one pass may lean to the first parent, which it is shown first. D7 is open: after organ 1's receipt its trace model was found to lean toward Emerson and James for any modern-English text and to barely name Marcus, Montaigne or Thoreau; this control is built to absorb the lean, and pairs without Emerson or James may show little.
seenBeforeSeal: all of organ 1: its cards, its 200 answers, the judge's readings of them, its receipt (7 of 7 held) and, after the receipt, where the trace model sent every answer. No breeding prompt has been sent, no child maxim written, no child or cross answer written, and no organ 2 batch judged.
